title: Flight Control Automation Engineer (m/f/d)
description_clean: As a Flight Control Automation Engineer, you will play a key role in our mission aircraft team and ensure seamless operation and interaction of complex aircraft functions. title: Doctorant(e) - "Vers un bâtiment low-tech : caractériser et réduire les dépendances liées à la maintenance et à l'entretien du bâti face au changement climatique"
description_clean: Rejoindre Mines Saint-Étienne, c’est s’engager dans une institution où la science et l’innovation bâtissent un avenir plus durable. Une école d’excellence où chacun a l’opportunité de révéler son plein potentiel et de contribuer à relever les défis de demain.Classée parmi les meilleures écoles d’ingénieurs en France et reconnue mondialement, notre école, membre de l’Institut Mines-Télécom, forme les talents de demain tout en contribuant activement à relever les grands défis industriels, numériques et environnementaux. Avec nous, vous intégrez une communauté de 500 collaborateurs, 2500 étudiants, et participez à un projet ambitieux : conjuguer excellence académique, recherche d’avant-garde et impact sociétal positif.L’Institut Mines-Télécom fédère les grandes écoles françaises autour des défis industriels majeurs, numériques, énergétiques et écologiques. Avec ses 8 Grandes Écoles publiques et 2 écoles filiales, il est le premier institut public dédié aux ingénieurs et managers. Ensemble, nous imaginons et construisons un avenir durable, en formant les acteurs qui façonneront les transitions de demain.Transitions numériques, écologiques, industrielles : les grands défis de notre époque sont aussi ceux de l’Institut Henri Fayol.Ici se mêlent Informatique, Sciences des données, Management, Sciences humaines et sociales, Génie environnemental pour penser les systèmes complexes de demain : territoires, entreprises, filières industrielles. 📊 Résilience, performance, durabilité… Nous développons et expérimentons en lien étroit avec les acteurs socio-économique pour répondre aux exigences des transitions actuelles.✨ Une recherche interdisciplinaire à fort impact, où l’humain est toujours au centre. Cette thèse de doctorat sera rattachée au département Génie de l'Environnement pour les Organisations (GEO), membre du Laboratoire CNRS UMR 5600 Environnement Ville et Société (EVS). Pour répondre aux enjeux des transitions écologique, énergétique et industrielle, le département GEO accompagne les acteurs des territoires (acteurs publics et privés) vers une meilleure prise en compte des enjeux environnementaux et de résilience territoriale. Il s'attache ainsi à apporter des solutions nouvelles en matière d'analyse, de modélisation et d'évaluation environnementale des systèmes industriels et territoriaux dans un double contexte d'industrie des futurs et de villes et territoires soutenables.🏠 Contexte Présentation du sujetLe changement climatique met en lumière, comme l'a fait auparavant la crise COVID, les vulnérabilités et liens de dépendance généralisée de nos modes de vie envers les infrastructures, les chaînes de valeur, et modes d'organisation économique et technique, éléments souvent déconnectés de l'usager final, de ses besoins et des conditions d'occupation. Pour le secteur du bâtiment, Cimerman (2023) évoque une tendance depuis plusieurs décennies de « simplification cartésienne » de la conception et de l'opération du bâti. Celle-ci se traduit notamment par le développement d'un imaginaire de « bâtiment-machine », se traduisant par une superposition d'éléments techniques complexes (chauffage, ventilation, climatisation), susceptibles d'être pilotés au travers d'outils informatiques et d'une gestion centralisée optimisée (Cimerman, 2023).Face aux enjeux posés par le changement climatique, deux voies opposées d'adaptation du bâti se dessinent. La première, actuellement dominante, consiste à prolonger cet imaginaire de « bâtiment-machine », rationalisable, mesurable et optimisable, et ce notamment au travers du développement du « smart-building ». Cette approche technosolutionniste apporte des réponses clés-en-main (capteurs, outils de pilotage centralisés, etc.) aux gestionnaires et usagers de bâtiments. Néanmoins, elle présente certains défis pour leur maintenance et leur entretien. Nous pouvons citer le recours massif aux nouvelles technologies, coûteuses, complexes, rapidement obsolètes et dont la fabrication repose en grande partie sur des ressources finies. Cela pose de plus les questions centrales des compétences, de la délégation du savoir et des outils associés à des opérateurs experts externes.En contrepoint à la première voie, une seconde approche, encore marginale, émerge : celle d'un « bâtiment low-tech ». Popularisée ces dernières années en France par Philippe Bihouix (Bihouix, 2014), la low-tech questionne le rapport à la technologie et aux différentes formes de dépendances qu'elle génère (Tanguy et al., 2023). Dans le secteur du bâtiment, l'application de cette démarche renvoie souvent à la dépendance à la ressource (énergie et matière) : repenser les usages, l'origine des matériaux (réemployés, biosourcés) ou encore la simplicité de l'équipement utilisé. Bien que nécessaires, ces travaux s'intéressent pourtant peu à d'autres formes de dépendances associées à la technique, au titre desquelles nous pouvons citer la dépendance aux savoirs et aux formes d'organisation sociale et économique qui conditionnent l'adéquation, la pérennité et l'efficacité des solutions proposées.Cette thèse offre ainsi une immersion concrète dans les questions d'adaptation du parc bâti au changement climatique par la « lowtech » à l'interface entre sciences de l'ingénieur et sciences humaines et sociales. Les compétences et l'expérience acquises trouveront une résonance particulière dans un secteur en pleine mutation, où la maîtrise des dépendances techniques, économiques et organisationnelles devient un enjeu central pour la soutenabilité des bâtiments et de leur exploitation.Contexte scientifiqueLa littérature consacrée à la low-tech s'est structurée ces dernières années autour d'une critique de la fuite en avant technologique et des dépendances qu'elle engendre (Bihouix, 2014 ; Tanguy et al., 2023). Appliquée au bâtiment, cette littérature reste toutefois majoritairement centrée sur la phase de conception et sur la dépendance à la ressource : sobriété énergétique, choix de matériaux biosourcés ou réemployés, réduction du niveau d'équipement technique.Deux angles morts en découlent. Le premier concerne la phase d'exploitation : la maintenance et l'entretien, qui représentent pourtant l'essentiel de la durée de vie d'un bâtiment et conditionnent la performance réelle des solutions installées, sont peu traités comme objet de recherche à part entière. Le second concerne la nature même des dépendances étudiées. Au-delà de la ressource, la conduite d'une opération de maintenance mobilise des savoirs et savoir-faire, des outils de diagnostic, des pièces détachées, des prestataires et des chaînes d'approvisionnement, ainsi que des cadres contractuels et réglementaires. Ces dépendances d’ordres cognitives, organisationnelles, économiques restent largement implicites et sous développées dans les travaux existants.La caractérisation de ces dépendances soulève par ailleurs une question d'échelle. Analysée au seul niveau du bâtiment, la maintenance apparaît comme une somme d'opérations techniques ; replacée à l'échelle urbaine, elle révèle des réseaux d'acteurs, des filières, des compétences localement disponibles ou absentes, et des effets de dépendance mutualisés.Contexte opérationnelDu côté des acteurs institutionnels et économiques, de nombreux outils accompagnent aujourd'hui la gestion technique du patrimoine bâti. Nous pouvons citer :les outils de gestion de maintenance assistée par ordinateur (GMAO) et les plateformes de gestion technique du bâtiment (GTB) ;les démarches de modélisation des données du bâtiment (BIM d'exploitation, jumeaux numériques) et les labels associés à la connectivité des bâtiments ;les contrats d'exploitation et de maintenance externalisés, et les dispositifs de garantie de performance énergétique ;les démarches et retours d'expérience issus de la mouvance low-tech (chantiers démonstrateurs, guides praticiens, réseaux associatifs).Ces dispositifs partagent une orientation commune : ils visent à optimiser la conduite de la maintenance, rarement à interroger les dépendances qu'elle installe. Les démarches low-tech, à l'inverse, portent cette interrogation mais restent au stade de l'expérimentation ponctuelle, sans cadre d'évaluation partagé ni capacité de généralisation à l'échelle d'un parc ou d'un territoire.Il en résulte, en l'état des connaissances aussi bien scientifiques qu'opérationnelles, qu'il n'existe pas de méthode permettant de rendre visibles et de qualifier les dépendances associées à la maintenance et à l'entretien des bâtiments, ni d'évaluer dans quelle mesure une approche low-tech permettrait de les réduire.🎯 Ce que nous attendons de vousDémarche de la thèseL'objectif principal de cette thèse est de caractériser les apports d'une approche low-tech pour cartographier et maîtriser, sinon réduire, les différentes formes de dépendances associées à la maintenance et à l'entretien des bâtiments.Les dépendances analysées s'appuieront sur les techniques, pratiques, outils et réseaux en lien avec la maintenance qui seront mis en évidence dans les deux autres thèses du projet PERENNIS. Cette thèse s'inscrit donc en complète continuité de ces deux travaux.Dans un premier temps, il s'agira de construire un cadre d'analyse des dépendances liées à la maintenance du bâtiment, articulant quatre registres : les ressources (énergie, matière, pièces détachées), les savoirs et savoir-faire, les acteurs et leurs relations contractuelles, et les réseaux techniques et logistiques. Cette phase s'appuiera sur une revue de la littérature scientifique et « grise », sur un benchmark des pratiques et outils de maintenance existants, et sur des entretiens avec les acteurs du secteur (gestionnaires de patrimoine, bailleurs, mainteneurs, bureaux d'études, collectivités).Dans un deuxième temps, ce cadre sera mobilisé pour caractériser et rendre visibles les schémas de dépendance à l'échelle urbaine, sur un ou plusieurs territoires d'étude. Il s'agira notamment d'identifier les sources de données mobilisables pour objectiver ces schémas, de qualifier les points de fragilité et d'apprécier leur variabilité selon les typologies de bâtiments et les configurations d'acteurs.Dans un troisième temps, des stratégies prospectives low-tech de maintenance et d'entretien seront proposées et instruites. Il s'agira de construire des scénarios contrastés, d'évaluer leur capacité à réduire la vulnérabilité technique, économique et sociale des opérations de maintenance dans un contexte d'adaptation au changement climatique, et d'en discuter la faisabilité et l'acceptabilité avec les parties prenantes concernées.Verrous scientifiques :Définition et opérationnalisation de la notion de dépendance appliquée à la maintenance du bâti, au-delà de la seule dépendance à la ressource (savoirs, acteurs, organisations, réseaux)Caractérisation et représentation de schémas de dépendance à l'échelle urbaine, à partir de données hétérogènes et partiellement indisponiblesÉvaluation prospective de stratégies low-tech en l'absence de retours d'expérience consolidés et de métriques établiesArticulation interdisciplinaire entre sciences de l'ingénieur et sciences humaines et sociales, et capacité à répliquer l'approche tout en visant la « parcimonie » des méthodes et modèlesObjectifs de développement durable rattachés :ODD 11 – Villes et communautés durables ·ODD 12 – Consommation et production responsablesODD 13 – Mesures relatives à la lutte contre les changements climatiques.  🔍 Ce que nous recherchonsFormation : Bac +5 en ingénierie généraliste, sciences de l'environnement, génie civil ou énergétique du bâtiment, géographie/aménagement, ou discipline connexe. title: CENTRALE LYON - Post-doctoral researcher (12 months) Mathematics of energy-efficient AI: diffusion models on emerging hardware
description_clean: The question Generating one image with a diffusion model means evaluating a large neural network tens to hundreds of times. That repetition is where the energy goes, and it is part of why data-centre demand is now visible at grid scale: the Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory puts US data-centre electricity use at 176 TWh in 2023, 4.4 % of national consumption, a figure that more than doubled since 2017 largely because of AI servers, and projects 325–580 TWh by 2028. Emerging hardware attacks exactly this primitive: analog in-memory computing, silicon photonics, ferroelectric devices and stochastic computing perform the underlying matrix–vector products at lower energy than digital CMOS, under conditions on scale and precision, but return a perturbed result. The usual objection is that nobody can say in advance how much perturbation a model tolerates. In EMMA, this opportunity is pursued through a PCM-based photonic matrix–vector engine as the primary demonstrator, complemented where appropriate by FeFET-based analog computing, so that device-level non-idealities are treated as explicit design parameters rather than as after-the-fact implementation losses. Diffusion models are an unusual case in which that question has a mathematical answer: their convergence theory bounds the discrepancy between the generated and target distributions by three terms, of which only one, the L 2 error of the learned score, depends on the hardware. That side is now in good shape: for stochastic samplers, bounds linear in the dimension under minimal assumptions on the data; for deterministic samplers, a matching theory under regularity. What is missing is the bridge. The theory is parameterised by a score error, the hardware literature by conductance noise, effective number of bits and photons per multiply–accumulate; nobody has written the map between them, in either direction. The quantisation literature for diffusion models reports image-quality scores; the induced L 2 score error, in the form the convergence theory needs, is directly measurable and goes unreported. One open sub-question sets the direction: the distinction between an error redrawn at each evaluation, as in stochastic computing, and an error frozen at write time, as in deterministic quantisation, has been settled in one setting only, and not the one hardware lives in; carrying it over is what this position exists to do. The work is judged on one concrete outcome. For at least one architecture, we want to show that theenergy gain from moving the score evaluation off digital CMOS is real, measured where it survives integration and not extrapolated from a single tile, and that it is paid for by a loss in sample quality that is small and, above all, tunable: a knob the designer sets, whose position the theory predicts rather than discovers afterwards. What you will do The work is organised in four packages, summarised below; the full research programme is available from the supervisors on request. 1. Make the score error measurable, starting from Gaussian targets where the whole error decomposition is closed-form. You will report the induced score error for a given perturbation of the network’s arithmetic, the number the theory needs and the quantisation literature does not report. 2. Map device physics onto the theory. Propagate the published error models for the technologies INL works on through the score network into an explicit score-error budget, separating what is proved from what is measured. 3. Extend the guarantees. Existing bounds assume a deterministic oracle, or a benign randomised one; extend them to error that is part frozen at write time and part redrawn at each call, and settle, on the way, which process the score error should be controlled along. 4. Co-design with INL, and deliver the proof of concept. Turn the score-error budget into an energy– accuracy frontier for INL’s PCM-based photonic matrix–vector engine, using device-calibrated circuitlevel models; a FeFET-based analog alternative may be considered where appropriate. Jointly vary sampler steps, stochastic bitstream length and effective precision to identify an operating point predicted to yield a real energy advantage over digital CMOS at a small, tunable loss in sample quality. The result is a frontier predicted from mathematical and hardware models, then verified against calibrated measurements. A clear negative answer is more useful to us than a vague positive one: a negative result on point 3 leaves points 1 and 2 intact and turns point 4 from a prediction into a measurement.  Who we are looking for Required • A PhD in applied mathematics, statistics, machine learning, electronic engineering, computer science or a closely related field, obtained (or with the defence scheduled) before the start of the contract. • A strong foundation in probability and stochastic analysis, numerical analysis, optimisation, or machine learning: SDEs, Girsanov’s theorem, time reversal of diffusions, with the ability to apply it rigorously to diffusion or other generative models. • Familiarity with the convergence theory of sampling algorithms, or the demonstrated capacity to acquire it quickly, for example through Langevin/MCMC analysis, optimal transport or concentration of measure. • Solid scientific computing (PyTorch or JAX), and the habit of writing code others can run. Ability and motivation to work across mathematical modelling and hardware-aware AI. • Working English; French is not required. Valued, not required Prior work on diffusion or score-based generative models; numerical analysis of finite-precision arithmetic. Familiarity with hardware-aware machine learning, approximate or stochastic computing, analogue in-memory computing, device modelling, circuit simulation, photonics, ferroelectric devices, or energy modelling. Experience linking model accuracy or robustness to implementation non-idealities, such as quantisation, noise, drift, variability, finite precision, or correlated errors. Evidence of interdisciplinary research, for example work at the interface of mathematics, machine learning, devices, circuits, architectures, or electronic-design automation. No hardware experience is expected or needed to apply.What matters most We are seeking a researcher who wants to explore how to turn physical constraints into mathematical and architectural design parameters. The project does not require prior laboratory hardware experience: INL provides device expertise, measured characteristics and modelling infrastructure. However, the successful candidate must be prepared to engage critically with non-ideal analog, photonic and ferroelectric accelerators, and to work with both supervisors to connect device-level error mechanisms, score-error guarantees and the energy–quality trade-off of diffusion-model inference. Candidates with a primarily mathematical background and strong curiosity for hardware are welcome, as are candidates from AIhardware, device-modeling, circuit, architecture or EDA backgrounds who have the stochastic-analysis maturity needed to develop the theory. The decisive criterion is the ability to make the mathematics and hardware inform one another, producing predictions that are quantitative, testable and relevant to an energy-efficient accelerator demonstrator.What we offer • A real double supervision, with weekly meetings that alternate between ICJ and INL. The two laboratories are on the same campus, five minutes apart on foot. • A question publishable on both sides: mathematics journals for the theory, design and hardware venues for the co-design. • Involvement in INL’s design–technology co-optimisation work through the PEPR Électronique CHOOSE project, and contact with the group’s ferroelectric and photonic device work (FVLLMONTI, Ferro4EdgeAI). • Support for conference travel and open-access publication, funded by the two host laboratories, and the career-development measures the establishment provides for post-doctoral researchers. • Practical help for international recruits through Espace ULYS, the EURAXESS service centre for Université de Lyon: visas, housing, health cover, banking, schooling. Conditions Twelve-month fixed-term contract under French public law, full time (1 607 h annual reference), 25 working days of annual leave plus the RTT days of the establishment’s scheme. Affiliation to the régime général for health and to IRCANTEC for supplementary pension; employer contribution to complementary health cover under the scheme in force at the establishment; 75 % reimbursement of publictransport season tickets, up to the statutory ceiling. The exact number of RTT days is set by the establishment.Find Jobs in France on Arbeitnow

Founded in 2012, Mirakl has been at the forefront of marketplace innovation, empowering every business to compete in the platform economy.Today, Mirakl's operating system combines an enterprise marketplace solution (Mirakl Platform) that enables retailers and B2B organizations to launch, scale, and operate marketplaces and dropship, AI-powered multichannel selling (Mirakl Connect), retail media (Mirakl Ads) and an agentic commerce infrastructure (Mirakl Nexus).With dual headquarters in Boston and Paris, Mirakl helps a global ecosystem of 450+ marketplaces (B2C and B2B) and a network of over 100k third-party marketplace sellers. Brands like Macy's, Decathlon, Carrefour, Asos, and Airbus Helicopters use Mirakl to grow their businesses in new and remarkable ways.
For more information, visit www.mirakl.com.
Mirakl in Numbers:

🗓️ Founded in 2012 | Member of French Tech Next40
👥 750+ employees in 9 offices worldwide: Paris, Barcelona, Bordeaux, Boston, London, Munich, New York, Sydney, Tokyo

Our Values:
Working at Mirakl means accelerating your career alongside ambitious, passionate, and supportive colleagues. We're proud of the diversity of backgrounds, perspectives, and experiences that make our teams unique.
Our 5 values guide how we collaborate:

💡 Work Hard Together: Teamwork and collaboration are the foundation of our success
🏆 Get Things Done:  We prioritize action and efficiency for impactful results
🚀 Go Above & Beyond:  We tackle challenges proactively and always aim for excellence
🎓 Succeed Through Expertise: Knowledge sharing and continuous learning are core to our culture
🤝 Satisfy & Empower Clients: We're committed to our clients' success

  The Team You'll Join
You'll be part of our global Accounting team at Mirakl. The team operates on a global scope, ensuring the financial integrity of Mirakl's entities worldwide. Together, you'll be supporting accurate, timely financial reporting and contributing to the robustness of Mirakl's finance function as the company continues to scale.
Please note that this mission is a contractor/freelance opportunity and is entitled to 1-day remote work a week 
Your Impact

Lead monthly and annual close processes, including managing accounts for foreign subsidiaries and liaising with local accounting firms
Own fixed asset control (tangible, intangible, and internally generated assets), including depreciation calculations and reconciliation
Ensure payroll accounting accuracy by booking monthly payroll entries in collaboration with the Controlling team and verifying the consistency of payroll and social charges
Manage current tax compliance, including VAT declarations (France & international), CVAE, C3S, and DAS2, in coordination with the Tax department
Prepare balance sheet justifications, intercompany account reconciliations, and audit-ready files for statutory auditors

 
What You'll Bring to the Role
Experience:

3 to 5 years of experience in general accounting
Proven track record managing multi-entity and/or international accounting scopes
Experience preparing regulatory tax filings and working with external auditors

 
Skills:

Strong command of general ledger accounting and month-end close processes
Ability to manage intercompany transactions and foreign subsidiary accounts
Payroll accounting and social charges compliance
Tax compliance (VAT, CVAE, C3S)
Rigorous, autonomous, and comfortable working in a fast-scaling environment

 
 Tools Used

Oracle Suite (ERP)
AI-powered tools (including Dust)

 
 Languages

French: Full professional proficiency
English: Full professional proficiency

 
Compensation & Contract
This is a freelance / contractor engagement. Rate and terms are open to discussion based on experience and scope.
Our Hiring Process
We warmly encourage you to apply to any of our roles, even if you think you're not an exact match.
Please click the "Apply" button to submit your application. This helps us make the best possible assessment and get back to you as quickly as possible.
Interview steps:

30/45-minute call with a TAS to discuss your key projects, ask technical questions, and present the position in details
45-minute Google Meet business discussion with Manon, our GL Accounting Manager 
1 x 45-minute STAR interview to assess your alignment with our values and meet another stakeholder you'll be interacting with
We welcome collaborators with their diverse perspectives and experiences to power us forward. These often far exceed conventional job requirements and help us create a culture of continuous learning. Companies representing 10% of global market capitalization trust Odaseva, including Schneider Electric, Volkswagen and Robert Half.

Accounting & Treasury Management:


Post bank entries and perform daily/monthly bank reconciliations.


Manage vendor invoices via our digital processing tool, directing them through approval workflows.


Prepare payment runs, perform accounts payable reconciliation, and manage vendor follow-ups/relations.


Perform accounts receivable matching and reconciliation.


Perform payroll accounting entry integration.


Apply analytical accounting principles across your perimeter.




Asset Management, Tax & Group Reporting:


Perform fixed asset accounting, tracking, and reconciliation.


Prepare monthly closing operations (cut-off entries, accruals, VAT, exchange variance analysis, etc.).


Prepare French tax declarations (DAS2, VAT, and other local taxes).


Manage US Sales Tax compliance


Contribute to monthly financial reporting and participate in the Group consolidation process.


Ensure daily maintenance of accounting ledgers in compliance with company rules, accounting standards, quality, and deadlines.


Support annual statutory audit processes.




Projects & Change Management:


Actively lead or participate in high-impact finance projects, process automation, and system enhancements.


Embrace and drive change to support the scaling of our international finance organization.




Required Qualifications


Experience & Technical Skills:


Degree in Accounting or Finance (e.g., DCG, DSCG, or equivalent).


5+ years of experience in a similar accounting role within an international group or fast-paced environment.


Hands-on experience with NetSuite (familiarity with CSV imports, FAM module, Saved Searches, and multi-currency/multi-entity setups) is required.


Strong technical accounting expertise (Local GAAP, closing operations, fixed assets, French taxes).




Soft Skills & Mindset:


Appetite for Change & Project-Driven: You thrive in scaling, evolving environments and enjoy driving or contributing to major transformation projects.


Rigor & Organization: You believe structured methods and precision are the keys to operational success.


Language: Professional English proficiency (written and spoken) to interact effectively within a global team and environment.




Where you'll be

Based in Paris (75002), France.
Hybrid: 3 days in the office / 2 days remote work.
Full time permanent contract position.


Who We Are
At Odaseva, we believe in fostering an inclusive, supportive work environment where talented people can innovate and grow. Our culture is built on being smart, humble, hardworking, and above all—collaborative.
 
Our core values define who we are: Trust, Customer Centricity, Engagement, Excellence, Continuous Innovation, and Teamwork.

Part of the corpus comes from real floorplans as images and PDFs that have to become clean, standardized graphs. A large part will be synthetic, procedurally generated building graphs, geometry and rendered floorplans, with controlled variation in style, scan noise, annotations and furniture, each kept with its ground-truth graph automatically.You will think about the whole loop, from raw and synthetic data to a canonical structured representation, curation and validation, the training dataset, large-scale pretraining, evaluation, data ablations, and back to improving the generator and the data mixture. Explore strategies to expand the dataset with synthetic data.Canonical representation and curation. Define the standardized representation, then filter, deduplicate, quality-score and validate at scale, with versioning, provenance and lineage.Pretraining data and mixtures. Assemble the training datasets, design the mixture and the curriculum, and blend synthetic and real data for large-scale pretraining.Data ablations. Train models to learn which data actually helps, read the results, and feed them back into the generator and the mixture.Evaluation. Build the eval harness (datasets, metrics, regression tests, monitoring) that tracks data and model quality over time.What We Are Looking ForYou have built the dataset, not just trained on it. A track record where the data itself is the object: curation, filtering, deduplication, quality scoring, mixtures, synthetic generation.Strong engineering. Deep Python, clean and typed code, async and concurrency, distributed data pipelines, TDD culture.Nice to haveComputer vision and document understanding, images to structured output, OCR, layout extraction, segmentation, geometry extraction, vectorization, raster to vector, image to scene graph, 3D or CAD.Graph and structured scientific data, molecular, protein or scene graphs, meshes, CAD, BIM, 3D geometry, or relational and structured world data.Synthetic worlds and simulation, a structured state to a simulator to a renderer to synthetic images with perfect labels, then a perception model, with an eye on the sim-to-real gap.Foundation models from scratch, real involvement in a large pretraining run, not only fine-tuning.Public evidence of data ownership, lead on a dataset, a Hugging Face release, a dataset card, a technical blog on your pipeline, or a talk on data curation or synthetic data.GIS and geometry, parcels, zoning layers, projections, computational geometry or constrained optimization.Multi-country data, heterogeneous sources, localization and varying rules.Why Join DavisOwn the data end to end, from the generator to the pretraining mixture, as the person who defines what the model learns from.Shape a foundation model from scratch, on a structured representation no one else is training on.Work on genuinely hard problems, image to graph, synthetic worlds and large-scale pretraining, with your work reaching clients within days.Competitive salary and meaningful equity, at a founding level, in an early-stage company.Join a world-class team, a mix of AI researchers, engineers and architects backed by world-class VCs.More information about Davis, the team and the market we're going after:TeamMehdi (Co-founder & CEO) grew up in a family of architects and has lived this problem firsthand. He is a repeat founder who bootstrapped his first startup at 20, and graduated from Sciences Po and HEC Paris. Amine (Co-founder & CTO) is an AI researcher from École Polytechnique who worked extensively on discrete diffusion and turned down a PhD with Google DeepMind to build Davis. They started working together in July 2025 at Entrepreneur First's first European residency, a two-month lock-in in a German castle.Today we are a team of twelve: technical profiles from Polytechnique, ENS and INRIA alongside architects and deep real estate expertise. We are small with an extremely high bar. If you want to work deeply on hard problems and see your work reach clients within days, you are the one we need.Why We Will WinReal estate is a $13 trillion industry that technology has largely bypassed. The professional services that feed it (design, engineering, feasibility, permitting) represent hundreds of billions in spend that no one has seriously automated.Proptech spent the last decade selling SaaS on the edges of these workflows. It did not work, for two reasons: no professional wants another tool to learn, and no tool can automate work that runs on expert judgment. Davis makes a different bet. We do not sell tools, we sell the work, AI-generated, expert-validated, delivered in days instead of weeks. Every project compounds our data advantage across typologies, geographies and regulatory contexts.Why No One Has Solved Architectural DesignReal estate development bleeds time and money in architectural design loops. Architects cycle through dozens of floorplan revisions to meet regulatory and client constraints, each round taking days, each missed constraint restarting the loop. Traditional CAD and BIM tools offer zero generative capability, and parametric tools only check constraints after generation, which leaves designs that frequently break under new zoning rules or irregular sites.Generative AI has the potential to solve this, but does not yet. Fine-tuning image diffusion models on floorplans produces layouts that look plausible but fall apart under scrutiny: hallucinated rooms, mislabeled spaces, code violations no architect would accept. Pixel-space models have no concept of what a wall is or why a corridor needs to connect two things. Compliance-guidance techniques typically require segmentation at each noisy timestep, compounding errors and making major edits impractical. These layouts may look plausible yet break building codes, or need heavy post-processing before they are usable.This is exactly the gap Davis closes. title: Senior Backend Engineer (f/m/d)
description_clean: Our OpportunityOver the past three years, Predium has built the leading real estate intelligence platform for ESG and value management in the DACH region - with the strongest names in the industry as customers: asset managers, housing companies, banks. Our customer base, our data, our credibility - that's valuable capital for the next step. Investment, credit, and asset management decisions in real estate are still made in Excel, case by case. We're now building the AI analyst that takes this work off people's hands - working directly on the customer's own data, scalable without adding headcount. We're well-funded, and we're bringing AI into real estate.Your MissionAs a Senior Backend Engineer, you own the systems behind our platform: the GraphQL API, the relational data model, the background processing that turns customer documents and spreadsheets into structured data, and the permission model that lets a single owner and a bank with hundreds of portfolios use the same product. Most of your work runs from schema design all the way to the resolver.You partner with product, design and other engineers to make sure we build what matters - not just what you have been told to do. You take real responsibility for production: when something is slow, you find out why, whether the answer is a bad query, application code or the infrastructure underneath.You also help us make AI reliable in production. Document extraction, long-running analysis jobs and agentic features are core to where the product is going, and we need people who make these workflows testable and dependable rather than impressive in a demo.Our company size of ~40 people ensures that the best idea wins and political discussions are kept aside. And every line of code helps to improve the carbon footprint of real estate properties.Tech stack: TypeScript (NestJS backend, React frontend), Hasura/GraphQL, PostgreSQL (multiple databases incl. PostGIS), queue-based job processing, AWS (ECS / Elastic Beanstalk, S3, SES, Textract), IaC, Claude but all agents welcomeWhat you'll ownBuild features across our Hasura GraphQL API, NestJS and Postgres. From schema design to resolver.Model complex real estate and ESG domains in relational schemas. We run several Postgres databases side by side (one of them geospatial), and schema decisions here have consequences but also positive impact.Own background processing: Excel imports, document extraction, long-running analysis jobs, 3D and image processing. Queues, retries, jobs that spawn other jobs - and figuring out what to do when step 3 of 7 fails at 2am.Develop our permission model. Customers range from a single owner to enterprises with organization/portfolio/building-level access.Integrate LLMs into backend workflows - especially document and data extraction - and make them reliable, verifyable and testable.Debug production. Navigate Grafana dashboards and traces to find out why something is slow or failing, whether in the app, the CI/build pipeline or the infrastructure.Spot overgrown or overly complex parts of the codebase and simplify them without being asked. Paying down complexity is part of the job.What success looks likeYou have shipped features end-to-end across schema, API and background processing that our customers actively use.Our async processing (imports, extraction, analysis jobs) is measurably more robust: fewer silent failures, clear retry and recovery paths, and observability that tells us what broke and why.You have taken ownership of at least one core area e.g. the permission model, the job orchestration layer or the LLM extraction pipeline and are the person the team goes to for it.You have raised the bar on testing and developer experience in the backend, and other engineers ship faster because of you.You are a trusted sparring partner for product and the team when we decide what to build and how.What it takesYou're strong with Postgres. Schema design comes naturally, you can read a query plan, and you know when the ORM is lying to you. Geospatial experience is a bonus, not a requirement.You're fluent in typed backend TypeScript. We work in NestJS and GraphQL every day; if your experience is in a comparable stack, that's fine, you'll pick it up fast.You've built real queue-based processing. You designed workers, dealt with retries and partial failures, orchestrated multi-step workflows.You've designed or worked with authorization for a multi-tenant product and know where it might get hairy.You'd rather have one integration test that hits a real database schema than ten unit tests mocking everything. You write the test that catches the broken migration.You treat production as a debuggable system. You can navigate dashboards and traces to figure out why something is slow, and you don't treat infrastructure as someone else's problem.You communicate clearly - with engineers, product and, when needed, directly with customers.You speak German at C1 level or better and English fluently. Our customers are German banks and asset managers, and you will talk to them.Bonus:AWS (S3, SES, ECS, RDS, …) and IaC.LLMs in production, especially document or data extraction and making it reliable for actual user workflows.Data pipeline work: staged, reproducible processing, dataset versioning.Mentoring or leading engineers, or wanting to grow into it.Debugging tooling and build issues, not just application code. Our toolchain moves fast and is occasionally non-standard.Why Predium?Stage: ~40 people, well-funded, on the way to defining the category. Early enough that a lot still needs to be built. Your contribution shows up directly, in revenue and in the product.Ownership: We don't manage your time, we measure your results. A definitive shift is currently happening. Corporates across the globe are no longer just reporting on sustainability; they are actively investing in it as a core financial and strategic asset.
At CEEZER, we are architecting the infrastructure for enterprise-grade Climate Performance Asset management, transforming how the world's largest companies source and manage carbon credits, Energy Attribution Certificates (EAC), and Sustainable Aviation Fuel certificates (SAFc).
Our platform gives the world’s most ambitious enterprises the data-driven precision, real-time monitoring, and framework-compliant reporting required to confidently deploy capital toward high-impact Climate Performance Asset portfolios and true, measurable climate action.
Tasks
Your mission
We are looking for a Tech Lead to join our engineering team. This role requires an ambitious technical leader who can architect scalable systems, navigate complex carbon data architectures, and drive engineering excellence. Moving beyond traditional software delivery, you will translate product vision into reliable technology, lead critical architectural decisions, and leave a lasting mark on our platform from day one.

Architect and scale a seamless B2B procurement platform, delivering an intuitive, enterprise-grade user interface designed for daily engagement and complex workflows.
Drive end-to-end technical strategy, design, and architecture, translating ambitious product requirements into performant, scalable features and microservices.
Lead by example with hands-on technical execution, authoring high-quality, maintainable code across our TypeScript, Node.js, and Next.js stack.
Cultivate engineering excellence across the team, providing high-impact mentorship, technical guidance, and rigorous code reviews to continuously elevate development standards.
Safeguard platform integrity, establishing robust security, reliability, and performance standards across our applications and core cloud infrastructure.
Partner closely with product, design, and cross-functional teams, evaluating trade-offs and technical permutations to engineer optimal, user-centric solutions.

Requirements
What you need to succeed

5+ years of professional software engineering experience, with a proven track record of technical leadership (2+ years) guiding teams through complex, full-lifecycle product deliveries.
Deep technical proficiency in TypeScript and the Node.js ecosystem, alongside extensive hands-on experience building modern, data-dense interfaces with React or Next.js.
Strong architectural expertise in RESTful API design, backend systems architecture, and relational data modelling (PostgreSQL experience preferred).
Demonstrated commitment to engineering rigour, with a deep understanding of software design patterns, enterprise web security standards, and modern development workflows (Git, feature branching).
Familiarity with cloud-native infrastructure and continuous deployment, including hands-on experience building and maintaining services on platforms like AWS.
Exceptional collaborative and communication skills, with the ability to articulate complex technical decisions, bridge alignment across product teams, and mentor engineers.
Basic familiarity with Python is a plus, or a strong technical curiosity to expand into auxiliary parts of our data processing stack.

Benefits
What's in it for you at CEEZER?

A mission that matters: Work alongside international teams combining finance, tech, and climate science professionals to direct capital toward the world's most critical climate assets.
Accelerated growth: We are scaling fast, and your career will too. Take opportunities to lead cross-functional initiatives and expand your strategic influence.
True ownership: We are building in a brand-new market, meaning many of our best practices don’t exist yet. If you see a better workflow, tool, or strategy, you have the autonomy and backing to build it.
An empowering environment: We bring together diverse global perspectives, knowing that solving complex climate challenges requires a wide mix of backgrounds and expertise.
Real enterprise impact: Transform how global corporates approach sustainability. CEEZER hosts 50Mt+ of vetted carbon credits across all pathways, all backed by sophisticated data and institutional-grade risk management.
A net-zero career: We practice what we preach. From your first day, we fully offset your personal and professional carbon footprint because sustainability is how we operate.

Experience working in international teams

Native-level German (spoken and written) for confident, natural customer conversations.
Willingness to wear many hats in an early-stage startup—CS, support, BD, product feedback, and ops in the same week.
Strong listening: ask useful questions, explain software patiently, and avoid jargon.
You learn products and processes fast and care why people (and systems) get stuck.
You stay organized and follow through across calls, tickets, BD threads, and internal ops.
Based in Germany.

Benefits

Work remotely within Germany.
Direct work with founders in a small team—high ownership, real impact.
Broad mandate across customers, product, and the company—not a siloed role.
Your feedback and work show up quickly in how Norman grows.

description_clean:
Introduction
We are smartmicro, the leading specialist in high-performance automotive and traffic radar- and radar/camera hybrid sensor technology. We design, develop and manufacture high-tech sensors for autonomous driving, intelligent traffic infrastructure and smart cities. Our mission is to make roads safer, enable autonomous driving in all-weather scenarios, optimize traffic flow for reduced travel times and enable greener, smarter cities.
We are a German company with international presence in the UK and in the US, while we are headquartered in Braunschweig for design, development and production.
We make the future of mobility a reality.
We are looking for an experienced Algorithm Engineer for Radar Tracking.
Your Tasks
In this role, you develop tracking and sensor fusion algorithms for radar and camera-based sensor systems used in intelligent traffic systems, smart mobility, ADAS-related applications, automated driving scenarios and airborne radar applications.

You develop, implement and validate algorithms for multi-object tracking, sensor fusion and statistical signal processing
You work on advanced tracking approaches such as extended object tracking, Bernoulli filters, Kalman filters, Bayesian filtering, probabilistic data association and related estimation methods
You work with real radar, camera and radar/camera fusion data and analyze algorithm performance in realistic traffic, mobility and airborne scenarios
You turn algorithmic concepts, prototypes and proof-of-concepts into robust, maintainable and testable software for product development and customer projects
You improve robustness, accuracy, runtime behavior and reliability of tracking and fusion algorithms under challenging real-world conditions
You define and use suitable test cases, metrics and validation methods to evaluate detection, tracking, fusion and object-level perception quality
Depending on the project, your work may contribute to applications such as intelligent traffic infrastructure, ADAS, automated driving, drone detection, UAV/UAS tracking and airborne radar systems.
You cooperate closely with embedded software, system engineering, testing and product teams to ensure reliable integration into our sensor platforms
Your work contributes to safety-critical and high-performance radar applications, for example by improving traffic flow, protecting vulnerable road users and enabling robust radar-based perception in airborne use cases

Your Strengths
We are looking for an engineer with proven professional experience in algorithm development, not only an academic background.

You have completed a Master’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, Robotics, Mathematics or a comparable technical field
You have some years of full-time professional experience in industrial or commercial algorithm/software development after graduation (Internships, thesis work, student jobs and purely university-based projects do not count toward this requirement)
You have practical experience with at least one of the following areas: multi-object tracking, sensor fusion, radar tracking, object-level fusion, nonlinear state estimation, statistical signal processing, perception algorithms or probabilistic methods
You are confident in programming with Python and C or C++ and can write structured, maintainable and testable code
You have a solid mathematical foundation, especially in linear algebra, statistics, probability theory, estimation theory and filtering methods
Experience with radar systems, camera systems, automotive sensors, ADAS, automated driving, intelligent traffic systems, embedded systems, real-time applications, drone tracking, UAV/UAS applications, airborne radar or radar altimeters is a strong advantage
Knowledge of tracking methods such as Kalman filters, EKF, UKF, particle filters, JPDA, MHT, Bernoulli filters, PHD filters or extended object tracking is beneficial
You are able to analyze complex technical problems independently and convert your findings into reliable software solutions
You work in a structured, delivery-oriented way and can balance technical quality with project constraints.
You communicate clearly in English; German language skills are an advantage

What you can expect from us

Innovation: latest technology, innovation and rapid development cycles, excellent work- and test equipment

About L1VE
L1VE is a growing media and technology company with locations in Berlin and New York. With immersive 12K, 3D and 360° streaming technologies and innovative live formats, L1VE is transforming the way people experience sports, music and entertainment.

As Head of Finance, you will act as a strategic partner to our CFO and executive team. You will translate the overarching finance strategy into scalable structures, robust planning and management models, and clear governance and reporting processes.
You will combine strategic foresight with strong execution skills: you will assess growth options, develop financial models and scenarios, and make opportunities, risks and economic implications transparent to management. In this role, you will work closely with our CFO in New York, the executive team, functional departments and internal and external finance partners.
Your Responsibilities

Develop and implement L1VE's finance architecture with a focus on growth, profitability, transparency and international scalability
Own integrated financial planning, business cases, financial models and scenarios as a basis for strategic decision-making
Evaluate business models, investments, partnerships and growth options, including their financial opportunities, risks and implications
Support financing rounds, investor readiness, due diligence and the preparation of strategic transactions in close coordination with the CFO
Manage management and investor reporting and further develop relevant KPIs, forecasts and governance structures
Manage interfaces with finance administration, accounting, tax advisors, auditors and other external finance partners

Your profile

At least seven years of professional experience in finance, including several years in a strategically responsible finance role - ideally as Head of Finance, VP Finance, Finance Director or in a comparable position within a startup, scale-up, technology, media or international corporate environment
Experience building scalable finance structures and working with integrated financial planning, business planning, financial modeling and management reporting
Sound knowledge of business performance management, governance, risk management and the evaluation of business models, investments and growth options
Experience with financing processes, investor reporting, due diligence or M&A is an advantage
Ability to structure complex financial topics clearly and act as a strategic sparring partner to the CFO, executive team and functional departments
Strong analytical and entrepreneurial thinking, a high degree of independence and a strong sense of ownership
Confident and practical use of AI tools in finance; you can demonstrate with specific examples which AI-supported solutions you have implemented and what additional value they created
Excellent written and spoken English and confident use of finance, reporting and collaboration tools; German language skills are an advantage

Why us?

You will shape the financial foundations of the next growth phase of an internationally active media and technology company.
You will work closely with our CFO in New York and the executive team and have a direct strategic influence.
You will have significant room to shape your work, short decision-making paths and the opportunity to build structures and systems that create lasting value.

Turn review insights into clear, actionable suggestions for product improvements and share them with the product team.

Flag relevant review themes to the marketing team to help shape messaging and campaigns.
Act as a central point for review management, coordinating feedback between the product, content and marketing teams.
Support the marketplace managers on execution projects, such as updating and optimising product listings.
Help out on a range of smaller tasks and projects across the team wherever an extra hand is needed.
Keep samples, records, trackers and documentation well organised and up to date.

Currently enrolled at a German university in a related discipline with at least 12 months of enrollment remaining.

Reliable, accountable, and self-motivated, with the initiative to take ownership of tasks and drive them to completion.


Highly organised and detail-oriented, with the ability to manage multiple priorities simultaneously.


Proficient in Microsoft Excel and comfortable learning new tools and systems.

Fluency in English is essential; German language skills are a plus.

Comfortable working for a brand that communicates openly and confidently about sexual wellness.

title: Product Manager, Delivery Promise
description_clean:
About Wolt
At Wolt, we create technology that brings joy, simplicity and earnings to the neighborhoods of the world. In 2014 we started with delivery of restaurant food. Now we're building the delivery of (almost) everything and you'll find us in over 500 cities in 30 countries around the world. In 2022 we joined forces with DoorDash and together we keep on dreaming big and expanding across the globe.Working at Wolt isn't always easy, but it's definitely exciting. Here you'll learn more, build more, and ship more than in most other companies. You'll be challenged a lot, but also have a lot of fun on the way. So, if you're a self-starter with drive and entrepreneurial spirit, this could be the ride of your life.We are looking for a Product Manager to join our Product Management organization, working with the Delivery Promise team. This is one of those parts of Wolt's business that people don't always realize the complexity of. Logistics is absolutely integral to Wolt, and doing it well can mean the difference between delivering blissful customer experiences efficiently and profitably vs. operational nightmares and a cacophony of late deliveries. 
The Delivery Promise team is in the Courier & Logistics Product group at Wolt. We're driving the future with estimates that fuel our growth, flywheel, shaping shopping decisions and streamlining deliveries. Our goal: boost Wolt's growth and profitability by delivering reliable, precise time estimates to customers and partners worldwide. In a nutshell, the team is responsible for crafting accurate and reliable time estimates that form a key part of the pre-checkout purchase experience for our consumers, right from discovery to checkout. We employ advanced machine learning models and innovative tools to craft delivery estimates experienced by consumers across all business lines for Wolt.   
As the Product Manager for the Delivery Promise team, your role will be integral in ensuring that we provide the best delivery estimates for our consumers while balancing the operational impact of fulfilling deliveries against the promised estimates. You will be contributing significantly to Wolt's goal of delightful customer experiences. 
Join us in shaping the future of delivery, where every delivery is an opportunity for delight and loyalty.
Our humble expectations
You could come to this role from various backgrounds, but ideally, you bring:

Plenty of previous experience as a Product Manager 
It's a plus for you if you have a background in Machine Learning or Data Science, since you would be focused on optimizing our estimates across markets and consumer cohorts.  
Proven track record in building products influencing cross-functional teams, including engineering, data, design, and operations.
High ownership and collaborative capabilities, making thoughtful decisions, and focusing on product details to ensure execution aligns with the vision.
Strong ability to define, execute, and measure meaningful OKRs, ensuring alignment with company-wide goals and fostering bottom-up alignment from your team.
Ability to focus on the bigger picture, creating solutions that benefit couriers, operations, and customer experiences across the organization.
Excellent stakeholder management skills, able to work effectively with diverse internal teams and external partners, while confidently engaging with leadership in a high-visibility role.

title: Senior Business Intelligence Lead (all genders)
description_clean: Your MissionEV charging is evolving from a niche technology into everyday infrastructure. As reev grows, teams increasingly need reliable, consistently defined metrics. Today, different dashboards, reporting dates, filters, and assumptions can produce different answers to the same business question. This role addresses the problem - not by building more dashboards, but by creating a shared and trustworthy data foundation. The goal is to establish clear definitions and consistent metrics so that teams and leadership can make informed decisions based on the same numbers. Someone who understands that unclear definitions, rather than a lack of data, are often the real problem can make a significant impact in this role. You own the certified layer, the single, agreed upon version of every core metric that reev runs on. You connect the definition, the data model, and the delivery. Check the results carefully. What this role is not You will not be the central owner of every dashboard request. Teams remain responsible for their own dashboards, analyses, and data models built on their data contracts. title: AI Growth Marketer (m/w/d) - remote
description_clean: Deine RolleWir sind ein kleines, agiles Marketing-Team. Jede und jeder übernimmt hier Ownership, entwickelt eigene Strategien und setzt sie selbst um. Seit wir konsequent mit AI arbeiten, sehen wir deutlich mehr Chancen zu wachsen, als wir bisher angehen können. Deshalb holen wir jemanden dazu, der sich alles übergreifend ansieht, die größten Hebel erkennt und sie selbst in die Hand nimmt.Du verantwortest Growth-Projekte end-to-end, auf bestehenden Kanälen und auf neuen, die Du selbst findest. Du baust selbst, stellst selbst live in der App, im App Store oder auf der Website, und wertest die Daten danach aus. Die Wege sind kurz, der komplette Projektzyklus liegt bei Dir.Deine Aufgaben:Chancen in unseren Produkten finden. Du gehst regelmäßig durch Website, App Stores, Content, Jobboards und den Funnel bis Premium und findest die Stellen mit dem größten Hebel für Registrierungen und Umsatz.Chancen im Markt erkennen. Du schaust genauso nach außen: Welche Trends und Plattformen bewegen unsere Zielgruppe gerade, welche Segmente oder Märkte lohnen einen Einstieg, welche Wachstumskanäle sollten wir aktivieren, die wir heute nicht nutzen, und was machen Wettbewerber.Chancen bewerten und priorisieren. Du schätzt vorher ab, was realistisch drin ist und was es bringt, und bringst eine Shortlist ins Team. Selbst bauen und selbst live stellen. Du baust Landing Pages, Tests und Kampagnenbausteine mit AI und veröffentlichst sie selbst. Kein Ticket bei Engineering, kein Warten auf Design, keine Warteschlange. Testen und messen. Du setzt A/B-Tests auf der Website, in den App Stores und auf unseren weiteren Plattformen auf, wertest sie sauber aus und iterierst. App Store Optimisation. Du testest Screenshots, Icon, Titel und Beschreibungen laufend weiter.Akquisition und früher Funnel. Dein Fokus liegt auf der Gewinnung neuer Nutzer. Gemeinsam mit dem Product Team bewertet Ihr, welche Zielgruppen und Kanäle den besten LTV bringen, und verbessert danach die Signup- und Activation-Flows im frühen Funnel.Copy und Botschaften. Du formulierst, was StudySmarter Lernenden bringt, so dass es bei unserer Zielgruppe ankommt und konvertiert. Headlines auf Landing Pages, Ad-Copy, Video-Skripte, Plakatmotive und mehr. Content und Kampagnen mit AI. AI-Content-Projekte, Markenaufbau für unsere Jobboards, Out-of-Home-Kampagnen.Love Brand aufbauen. Du entwickelst gemeinsam mit uns eine globale Love Brand für B2C und B2B und prägst mit, wie StudySmarter aussieht und klingt.Was die Rolle nicht istKeine klassische Designstelle. Geschmack und Markenurteil sind wichtig, die handwerkliche Ausführung läuft über AI und Freelancer.Kein Performance-Marketing-Job. Kanäle, Budget, Bidding und Attribution liegen an anderer Stelle im Team.Keine Briefing-Rolle. Du machst die Arbeit selbst, statt sie weiterzugeben.Keine Product-Rolle. Du bist kein Product Manager. Du trägst die Nutzerakquisition und arbeitest dafür eng mit dem Product Team zusammen, ohne Produktverantwortung zu übernehmen.Keine Führungsrolle. Du arbeitest eng im Marketing-Team und gemeinsam mit dem Gründerteam, führst aber keine eigenen Mitarbeitenden. Dafür deutlich mehr Gestaltungsspielraum.Was du für diese Rolle brauchstStarke AI-Skills. Du arbeitest täglich mit AI-Tools wie Claude Code, Codex oder ähnlichen, dazu mit Agents und Automatisierung. Du baust eigene Seiten, Tools und Workflows und bringst sie selbst live, statt nur Prompts zu schreiben.Starkes Copywriting und Storytelling. Du schreibst Texte, die auffallen und konvertieren, und findest dieWorte, die bei Schülerinnen, Schülern und Studierenden ankommen. Du denkst in Geschichten und Nutzen, nicht in Feature-Listen.Eigenständigkeit und Tempo. Du nimmst ein Thema und bringst es durch. Zehn Dinge live und gemessen sind Dir lieber als zwei perfekte. Zahlenverständnis. Du liest Funnel selbst, arbeitest in Analytics-Tools und bewertest Tests ehrlich, auch wenndas Ergebnis gegen Deine Idee spricht.Ein Auge für Design. Du erkennst, was gut aussieht und was nicht, und kannst einschätzen, wann DesignConversion bringt und wann es nur Dekoration ist. Figma ist Dir vertraut.Marketing-Grundverständnis. Du weißt, wie Paid, SEO und Lifecycle grundsätzlich funktionieren. Die Details der einzelnen Kanäle lernst Du bei uns.Zwei Dinge sind Voraussetzung:Deutsch auf Muttersprachniveau. Du schreibst für unsere Zielgruppe auf Landing Pages, inAds, in den App Stores und offline. Ohne echtes Sprachgefühl funktioniert das nicht.Eigene Projekte, die Du zeigen kannst. Seiten, Tools, Content, Nebenprojekte. Das sagt unsmehr als ein Lebenslauf.Wir schauen auf Skills, Execution, Tempo, Kreativität und Ambition, nicht auf die Anzahl der Berufsjahre. StarkeAbsolventinnen und Absolventen sind ausdrücklich willkommen, ebenso Profile mit einigen Jahren Erfahrung.Warum StudySmarter?Remote arbeiten, so viel Du möchtestModernes Büro mit Terrasse, mitten im Münchner WerksviertelBeteiligung am UnternehmenserfolgAusstattung nach Deiner WahlDirekter Draht zu den FoundernEGYM Wellpass für Sport und GesundheitObst, Säfte, Porridge-Bar und Getränke-FlatrateRegelmäßige Team-Events, Sommer- undWeihnachtsfeierBudget für Fortbildung und WeiterentwicklungEin Umfeld, in dem Du AI nicht rechtfertigen musstDeine BewerbungSchick uns Deinen CV und Links zu AI-Projekten, die Du verantwortet hast. Ein Anschreiben ist optional. Und zeig uns etwas, das Du in den letzten drei Monaten mit AI gebaut hast. Ein paar Absätze oder ein kurzes Video genügen.Wir schätzen unterschiedliche Erfahrungen und Perspektiven und ermutigen alle Menschen, sich zubewerben, auch wenn nicht jede Anforderung perfekt erfüllt ist. Wenn Du unsicher bist, ob Dein Profil passt,bewirb Dich und lass es uns beurteilen.Find more English Speaking Jobs in Germany on Arbeitnow

title: Senior Engineering Manager, Product Engineering
description_clean: Location: Remote (EMEA) · Germany/Munich preferred - CET/CEST time zoneHi — I'm Grigory, co-founder and CTO at Secfix.At Secfix we're building security compliance systems for teams and agents to become and stay compliant with less effort. We're already the category leader in Europe. AI is changing how software gets built, and we're shaping the tools this new era requires.I've spent most of my career believing that the best engineering leaders aren't the ones who run the most meetings. They're the ones who make everyone around them faster, clearer, and more proud of their work — and they can do that because they've been through the hard technical problems themselves.Since we started, I've done the engineering management myself: 1:1s, hiring, design reviews, performance conversations. The team is 8 engineers and 2 product designers, and I'm spread across too many things. If we were a football team, we'd be a good regional side that just made it to the Bundesliga — talented, hard-working, winning quite a few games. Now we need a coach who's played at Champions League level and can take us there to win every week.That means a strong engineering manager who can still ship. Someone who owns the technical decisions, sets the pace, and has product taste — who notices when a feature takes three weeks that should take one, and when it ships on time but isn't good enough. You won't ship weekly — you'll need focus — but you'll build with the team often enough to know the playbook still works.You'll work directly with me. Two things matter most here: speed and taste. Most teams pick one. We need both to win.— GrigoryWhy Secfix existsOver 1.78 million SMBs in Europe need to comply with security frameworks — ISO 27001, GDPR, TISAX, SOC 2 — just to sell to enterprise customers. The process is manual, painful, and takes over a year. We automated it.Our platform integrates with a company's full tech stack — AWS, Azure AD, Jira, GitLab, GCP, and more — automatically extracts compliance evidence, and guides teams to certification in weeks instead of months. Our fastest customer was certified in 4 weeks instead of the industry-standard 12+ months.We've raised €17M in total (€12M Series A), backed by Alstin Capital, Neosfer (Commerzbank), and Bayern Capital. We're on a profitable trajectory, growing fast, and building the team that will take us to own European market from SMBs to mid market.This space is not threatened by AI; it's amplified by it. Compliance requires deep domain expertise combined with automation. Our new AI product (CISO AI) is just getting started, and there's a huge amount of engineering work ahead: agentic workflows, intelligent evidence collection, context-aware policy generation, and more.What you'll actually do in the first 3 monthsThis isn't a role where you show up and start running standups. There are no standups. Here's how the first quarter goes:Month 1: Ship. Get into the codebase and ship a meaningful feature with AI alongside the team. You don't need to be the fastest engineer in the room, but the team needs to see that you can build at the level you'll ask of them and can ask the right questions.Month 2: Make the team faster. Find where features take three weeks that should take one, and fix it — in tooling, in how we review and test, or in who's working on what. Start regular 1:1s with each engineer, focused on weekly output, quality, and how well they use AI.Month 3: Own hiring. Take over engineering interviews and build a process that runs without my oversight. Design the technical challenges, run the screens, make the calls. The next people we bring in should raise the pace again. I will be there but switch my focus to final interviews.What will the role look like beyond the first 3 months?After the first quarter, the job is management and the technical decisions. You own how the team builds: how engineers test, how they review each other's code and security, how the team is organised, and who we hire next. We're 8 engineers and 2 product designers today and plan to be around 16 within 12 months — most of that hiring is yours to run.You won't ship weekly, but you'll build something with the team now and then, because that's how you know the playbook still gets things out the door. Our CS and Sales leaders work the same way — they still own a small slice of the IC work, so they have skin in the game.Here's what you'll be close to in the next months:Speed. You’ll refine our software development processes to keep the team operating at high velocity. Cycle time from spec to production is your number and accountability. Tooling, review flow, how work is split, who's on what — whatever moves it.Quality. Improve how engineers test and automate, how they review each other's code and security changes, and how the zero-bug policy survives a team of 20.Team and hiring. Team structure, growth conversations, the hiring process, and eventually the next manager.AI in the craft — and in the management. Engineers already work with an established set of encoded skills and rules — there's a whole playbook; you keep pushing that. Same for your own work: hiring, 1:1s, the recurring stuff.What success looks likeAt 6 months: The hiring process runs without me, and we've added 2 engineers through it. Sales, CS, and product all feel the difference in how fast we ship — and in quality.At 12 months: The team is around 12-16, the zero-bug policy is still holding at that size, and I'm not in the engineering critical path anymore. You've found and/or coached the EM Nr. 2 to support growth.How we workWe've written in depth about our engineering culture. Here's the short version — read the full articles linked below if you want the real picture.Focus is sacred. Engineers are in fewer than 2 hours of meetings per week. We write before we meet. We use Loom for async walkthroughs, Notion for specs, Gather for pairing, and Slack only for what's urgent or lightweight. We don't do status theatre. We wrote about our thoughtful communication and our remote culture; give it a read.To drive it home, here's a recent calendar of an engineer who has been with us for over a year:Small, temporary teams. A designer and two engineers. A backend engineer and a CS person. The group forms around the problem, ships, and dissolves. No standing squads, no permanent team structures — at least not yet. The people closest to the problem usually shape the solution.AI is already part of the craft. We use Claude for product design exploration and spec drafting. Customer feedback is signal, not instructions. Best products are built by people with great taste who treat feedback as signals, not KPIs. We stay close to customers — CS check-ins, support tickets, Mixpanel events, onboarding calls — but none of these sources makes the decision for us.This role is for you if:You've managed a real team and made it ship faster. But you're not scared of jumping into a pair programming session either.What we're looking forRequired8+ years as a software engineer, including 4+ years managing a team of 8+ and hiring for it yourselfYou've shipped AI features to production — retrieval, RAG, agentic workflows — and you know the difference between a demo that works and one that holds up on real customer dataProduct taste: a keen sense for what makes a product feel great, and the habit of saying so when it doesn'tYou've built and shipped with Claude Code and Cursor in real production work, and you have opinions about where AI helps and where it quietly creates debtYou're an engineer at heart. title: Product Engineer Procurement
description_clean:
Job Description

✨ A little about us
Container xChange is building the distribution channel for global container trading.
We operate in a huge, fragmented and still highly inefficient market. Our ambition is to make it dramatically easier to access the right inventory, compare opportunities, transact and fulfil container purchases across sellers and locations globally.
To win, we need to get a few things exceptionally right: more of the right containers, in the right locations, at better prices — from sellers who are fast, reliable and easy to trade with.
That is where you come in.
🧭 The Role
As Product Engineer – Procurement, you will own our Procurement function end-to-end in close collaboration with our CEO Christian.
This is a hands-on commercial builder role: you run Procurement, improve the economics, and build the processes, automations and product solutions that make the function scale.
You will start hands-on: run day-to-day procurement, work directly with sellers, negotiate prices and promotions, support Sales on supply opportunities and understand where our current processes work well — and where they break.
But your mandate goes further: Build a Procurement function that becomes a competitive advantage for xChange.
We want you to constantly ask: How can we improve the economics? How can we make this process faster? What can we standardize? What can we automate?
You will use Claude and other tools to build lightweight solutions yourself, experiment with deterministic and agentic automation, and work closely with Engineering where solutions need to become part of our core product.
Over time, repetitive operational work should decrease while your focus on Seller Performance, Procurement strategy, automation and product improvements grows.
📍 Location
This is a position based in Hamburg, where you will work closely with our Sales, Product and Engineering team as well as directly with our CEO Christian.
Requirements
🚀 Your Impact
Ultimately, your work should help xChange transact more containers at better margins, while allowing Procurement to scale without scaling manual work at the same rate.
You will:

Own and run day-to-day Procurement and tactical Seller Management, using what you learn from operating the processes yourself to continuously improve, streamline and automate the function.
Improve our buying economics and Seller Performance by identifying pricing opportunities, negotiating with sellers, driving promotions and improving listing quality, reply speed, release speed and reliability.
Use Claude and other tools as part of your day-to-day work to solve problems faster and improve our processes and systems.
Build lightweight, bootstrapped solutions yourself when they can solve an immediate problem — from deterministic workflows to agentic solutions.
Work closely with Engineering when those solutions need to become more robust, scalable or part of our core product.
Build a more systematic, data-driven view of Procurement, so we can identify and prioritize the biggest opportunities across our seller portfolio.
Drive larger strategic initiatives such as gatebuy, future pickups and new ways of sourcing inventory that help us build a structurally better trading engine.

🌟 What Makes You a Great Fit?
We are looking for someone who combines commercial intuition, strong execution and a product/automation mindset.
You are likely a great fit if you:

Get genuine satisfaction from negotiating a better deal and spotting commercial opportunities others might miss.
Have a passion for trading, pricing and markets — whether that comes from work, the stock market, sports betting or simply how you think.
Are commercially confident enough to own seller relationships, make decisions independently and push back when needed.
Perform well under pressure and at speed — matching the pace of Sales without sacrificing accuracy.
Are highly structured and operationally reliable: fast without becoming sloppy.
Enjoy getting your hands dirty and executing the work yourself.
Think beyond individual cases and naturally ask how a process can be improved at a system level.
Can balance short-term execution with long-term improvement — improving processes, automation and scalability over time.
Are data-driven and comfortable using metrics to identify opportunities.
Already use AI to solve real-world problems and are excited about building prototypes, workflows and automations.
Can translate a business problem into something Engineering can work with.
Have strong ownership, drive and the learning velocity to grow further into product and automation.

You do not need to be a software engineer. We care much more about your ability to understand a problem deeply, imagine a better solution, prototype where possible and collaborate effectively with Engineers.
Deep container knowledge and traditional Procurement experience are also not prerequisites.
This role might not be for you if…

You prefer having perfect information before making decisions — this role requires fast judgment under uncertainty.
You don’t enjoy working in a high-pressure, fast-moving commercial environment where Procurement needs to match the pace of Sales.
You prefer staying at one level of the problem rather than switching between what needs to happen now, what needs to change commercially, and what needs to improve in the process or product.
You prefer clearly bounded responsibilities over end-to-end ownership — we expect you to take decisions, push back on sellers when needed, and stay accountable until the issue is actually resolved.

👀 What to Expect

A rare combination of commercial and product ownership: You will understand and improve the full Procurement system — from the economics of individual trades to the processes and technology behind the function.
A role that evolves with you: You will initially spend significant time running Procurement hands-on. As you improve and automate the function, your role should increasingly shift toward Seller Performance, Procurement economics, product and automation.
Direct exposure to the business: You will work closely with our CEO Christian and have direct visibility into how supply, pricing and seller performance translate into containers transacted and margin.
Build rather than inherit: You are not joining a mature Procurement function with a fixed playbook. You will help define how Procurement at xChange should work in the future, from how we manage sellers today to how much of the function can eventually be automated.
AI as a real working tool: We expect you to use tools such as Claude to increase your own leverage and continuously challenge which parts of your job still need to be done manually.
The long-term opportunity is to help build a Procurement engine that becomes one of xChange’s core competitive advantages.
